(<reference osisRef="Dan.4.35">Da 4:35</reference>).<div eID="gen14080" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Isa.14.28-Isa.14.32">Is 14:28-32</reference>. Prophecy against Philistia.</title> <div sID="gen14081" type="x-p"/> To comfort the Jews, lest they should fear that people; not in order to call the Philistines to repentance, since the prophecy was probably never circulated among them. They had been subdued by Uzziah or Azariah (<reference osisRef="2Chr.26.6">2Ch 26:6</reference>); but in the reign of Ahaz (<reference osisRef="2Chr.28.18">2Ch 28:18</reference>), they took several towns in south Judea. Now Isaiah denounces their final subjugation by Hezekiah. <div eID="gen14081" type="x-p"/>
entries.99ea1bf23817cfad5872311dc9fbd898220d503e: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8597"/><div sID="gen14082" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8597"/><hi type="bold">28. In ... year ... Ahaz died--</hi>726 B.C. Probably it was in this year that the Philistines threw off the yoke put on them by Uzziah. <div eID="gen14082" type="x-p"/>
entries.5ee6dacf7a9bda3c05626a4dd3f9c5166911f18b: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8598"/><div sID="gen14083" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8598"/><hi type="bold">29. Palestina--</hi>literally, "the land of sojourners."<div eID="gen14083" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14084" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rod ... broken--</hi>The yoke imposed by Uzziah (<reference osisRef="2Chr.26.6">2Ch 26:6</reference>) was thrown off under Ahaz (<reference osisRef="2Chr.28.18">2Ch 28:18</reference>).<div eID="gen14084" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14085" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">serpent's root--</hi>the stock of Jesse (<reference osisRef="Isa.11.1">Is 11:1</reference>). Uzziah was doubtless regarded by the Philistines as a biting "serpent." But though the effects of his bite have been got rid of, a more deadly viper, or "cockatrice" (literally, "viper's offspring," as Philistia would regard him), namely, Hezekiah awaits you (<reference osisRef="2Kgs.18.8">2Ki 18:8</reference>). <div eID="gen14085" type="x-p"/>
entries.3020fe16132fd11d3f457aae2e39a9910dbe1c4d: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8599"/><div sID="gen14086" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8599"/><hi type="bold">30. first-born of ... poor--</hi>Hebraism, for the most abject poor; the first-born being the foremost of the family. Compare "first-born of death" (<reference osisRef="Job.18.13">Job 18:13</reference>), for the most fatal death. The Jews, heretofore exposed to Philistine invasions and alarms, shall be in safety. Compare <reference osisRef="Ps.72.4">Psa 72:4</reference>, "Children of the needy," expressing those "needy in condition."<div eID="gen14086" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14087" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">feed--</hi>image from a flock feeding in safety.<div eID="gen14087" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14088" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">root--</hi>radical destruction.<div eID="gen14088" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14089" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">He shall slay--</hi>Jehovah shall. The change of person, "He" after "I," is a common Hebraism. <div eID="gen14089" type="x-p"/>
entries.f7396ef704708a1ea89c7916873451c737db4dd1: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8600"/><div sID="gen14090" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8600"/><hi type="bold">31. gate--</hi>that is, ye who throng the gate; the chief place of concourse in a city.<div eID="gen14090" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14091" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from ... north--</hi>Judea, north and east of Palestine.<div eID="gen14091" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14092" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">smoke--</hi>from the signal-fire, whereby a hostile army was called together; the Jews' signal-fire is meant here, the "pillar of cloud and fire," (<reference osisRef="Exod.13.21">Ex 13:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Neh.9.19">Ne 9:19</reference>); or else from the region devastated by fire [Maurer]. Gesenius less probably refers it to the cloud of dust raised by the invading army.<div eID="gen14092" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14093" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">none ... alone ... in ... appointed times--</hi>Rather, "There shall not be a straggler among his (the enemy's) levies." The Jewish host shall advance on Palestine in close array; none shall fall back or lag from weariness (<reference osisRef="Isa.5.26">Is 5:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.5.27">27</reference>), [Lowth]. Maurer thinks the Hebrew will not bear the rendering "levies" or "armies." He translates, "There is not one (of the Philistine watch guards) who will remain alone (exposed to the enemy) at his post," through fright. On "alone," compare <reference osisRef="Ps.102.7">Psa 102:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.8.9">Ho 8:9</reference>. <div eID="gen14093" type="x-p"/>
